content: 1. Ethinylestradiol and Intestinal Flora Alteration: Ethinylestradiol levels may be reduced by altering the intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Ethinylestradiol and Olanzapine: Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of olanzapine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Ethinylestradiol and Otesaconazole: Otesaconazole may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. This interaction may enhance the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Consider starting with the lowest dose of the BCRP substrate or reducing its dose. 4. Ethinylestradiol and Paromomycin: Paromomycin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Ethinylestradiol and Penicillin G: Penicillin G aqueous can decrease ethinylestradiol levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially leading to oral contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Ethinylestradiol and Penicillin VK: Penicillin VK may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Ethinylestradiol and Pioglitazone: Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Ethinylestradiol and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Ethinylestradiol and Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Ethinylestradiol and Ramelteon: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Ethinylestradiol and Rasagiline: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of rasagiline by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, especially when used in combination with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 12. Ethinylestradiol and Ribociclib: Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Ethinylestradiol and Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Ethinylestradiol and Romidepsin: Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through receptor binding competition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Ethinylestradiol and Ropinirole: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of ropinirole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Ethinylestradiol and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 17. Ethinylestradiol and Rufinamide: Rufinamide decreases the effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Rufinamide is a weak inducer of CYP3A4 and may reduce the exposure of drugs metabolized by this enzyme. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Ethinylestradiol and Selegiline: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of selegiline by inhibiting its N-demethylation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Ethinylestradiol and Siltuximab: Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated during infection and inflammation. Caution is advised when coadministered with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 20. Ethinylestradiol and Somapacitan: Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of somapacitan through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring a higher growth hormone dose. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
